title: Plural 10: Plural-Only Nouns and the -анин / -янин Family
titleRussian: Множественное число 10: слова только во множественном и модель -анин / -янин
description: Two more irregular groups: nouns that exist only in the plural (часы́, но́жницы, де́ньги), whose genitive plural you must memorise, and the -анин / -янин nouns that drop -ин in the plural and take a zero genitive plural (англича́не → англича́н).
descriptionRussian: Ещё две неправильные группы: слова, которые существуют только во множественном числе (часы́, но́жницы, де́ньги), у которых нужно запомнить родительный множественного, и слова на -анин / -янин, которые теряют -ин во множественном и имеют нулевой родительный множественного (англича́не → англича́н).
intro: Two more groups, and both have the same practical problem: there is no singular to build the genitive plural from, so you memorize it directly. The plural-only nouns you have met since A1. The other group is a suffix that drops a whole syllable in the plural, which is what nationality and citizen words do. That group at least is consistent: its genitive plural is always a bare stem.
rules: Plural-only nouns have no singular form: часы́, но́жницы, очки́, де́ньги, су́тки, воро́та, штаны́, духи́, кани́кулы, джи́нсы. They decline as ordinary plurals.
Because there is no singular to build on, the genitive plural of plural-only nouns must be memorised directly: часо́в, но́жниц, очко́в, де́нег, су́ток, воро́т, штано́в, кани́кул.
Де́ньги inserts a fleeting vowel in the genitive plural to break the unpronounceable cluster: де́ньг → де́нег (нет де́нег).
The -анин / -янин singular drops the whole -ин syllable in the plural and adds -е: граждани́н → гра́ждане, англича́нин → англича́не, крестья́нин → крестья́не.
The genitive plural of the -анин / -янин nouns is the zero ending - no -ов, no -ей: гра́ждан, англича́н, крестья́н, славя́н, христиа́н.
examples: У меня́ нет часо́в. (I don't have a watch.) часы́ has no singular; gen pl часо́в (Family 4).
Ма́ша купи́ла но́вые очки́. (Masha bought new glasses.) очки́, a plural-only noun, acc = nom.
У студе́нтов нет де́нег. (The students have no money.) де́ньги → де́нег, fleeting vowel in the gen pl.
На пло́щади мно́го англича́н. (There are many English people in the square.) англича́нин → англича́не → англича́н, zero gen pl (Family 5).
В э́той стране́ живёт мно́го славя́н. (Many Slavs live in this country.) славяни́н → славя́не → славя́н, zero gen pl.
Все гра́ждане име́ют э́то пра́во. (All citizens have this right.) граждани́н → гра́ждане, the -ин-dropping plural.

tables.title: Plural-Only Nouns and Their Genitive Plural

items.prompt: У меня́ нет _____ — мо́жно посмотре́ть на твои́?
items.promptEnglish: I don't have a watch - can I check yours?
items.hint: Часы́ is a plural-only noun. After нет: gen pl.
items.explanation: Часы́ exists only in the plural (for the meaning 'watch / clock'). After нет the noun takes the gen pl: часо́в. The form часа́ exists but is the gen sg of час 'hour', a different word (два часа́).

items.promptEnglish: There were many English people at the station.
items.hint: Англича́нин is Family 5. The plural drops -ин; the gen pl is zero.
items.explanation: Англича́нин drops the -ин syllable in the plural: англича́не. The gen pl is the zero ending: англича́н. Англича́нинов and англича́нов both keep parts of the singular stem that the plural has already dropped, so neither exists.

items.promptEnglish: The students have no money at all.
items.hint: Де́ньги is plural-only; after нет, gen pl. Watch the fleeting vowel.
items.explanation: Де́ньги is a plural-only noun, and after нет it takes the genitive plural. The bare stem де́ньг ends in an unpronounceable cluster, so a fleeting vowel breaks it: де́нег. Де́ньг is the trap.

items.promptEnglish: Masha bought new trousers for running.
items.hint: Купи́ть + accusative. Штаны́ is plural-only; for an inanimate plural, acc = nom.
items.explanation: Штаны́ exists only in the plural (Family 4). The accusative of an inanimate plural equals the nominative: штаны́. Штана́ would be a singular for a word that has no singular.

items.promptEnglish: Russian peasants are sitting in the class.
items.hint: Subject role = nominative plural. Крестья́нин drops -ин and adds -е.
items.explanation: As the subject the noun is in the nominative plural. Крестья́нин drops the -ин syllable and adds -е: крестья́не. Крестья́н is the genitive plural (мно́го крестья́н), wrong for a subject; крестья́нинов and крестья́ны are invented forms.

items.hint: After две the noun is genitive singular. Неде́ля is a regular feminine noun here.
items.explanation: This item checks that you keep the regular number rule alongside the new words: после две the noun takes the genitive singular, неде́ли. (Кани́кулы itself is the plural-only subject; the verb agrees with it in the plural: дли́лись.)

blanks: Ма́ша забы́ла свои́ _____ до́ма. (Masha left her glasses at home.)
В э́той стране́ живёт мно́го _____. (Many Slavs live in this country.)
По́сле двух _____ пути́ они́ верну́лись. (After two days of travel they came back.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: (1) Забы́ть + acc; очки́ is a plural-only inanimate noun, acc = nom: очки́. (2) Мно́го + gen pl; славяни́н drops -ин and takes a zero gen pl: славя́н. (3) После двух + gen pl; су́тки is plural-only with the gen pl су́ток.
hints: Очки is plural-only; for an inanimate plural the accusative equals the nominative.
Many + countable plural takes the genitive plural; -янин drops -ин to a zero ending.
After 2 the noun is genitive... but суток is the plural-only genitive form here.

errorCorrection.sentence: В на́шем го́роде живёт мно́го славя́нов.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Many Slavs live in our city.
errorCorrection.explanation: Nouns in -янин drop the -ин syllable in the plural (славяни́н становится славя́не) and take a zero genitive plural: мно́го славя́н. Славя́нов keeps the singular -ян- and stacks -ов on top, which this closed family never does.

errorCorrection.sentence: Ле́том у нас три ме́сяца кани́кулов.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: In summer we have three months of holidays.
errorCorrection.explanation: Кани́кулы ('holidays') is a plural-only noun with a zero genitive plural: три ме́сяца кани́кул. Кани́кулов stacks the masculine -ов onto a word that takes the bare stem.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: We travelled for two full days.
errorCorrection.explanation: Су́тки ('a 24-hour day') is plural-only, and its genitive plural is the bare stem with a fleeting -о-: су́ток. Су́тков stacks -ов on top, which this word never takes.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Sharp scissors were lying on the table.
errorCorrection.explanation: Но́жницы is a plural-only noun, and as the subject it stands in the nominative plural но́жницы. Но́жницев grafts a regular masculine -ев ending onto the word and is not a real form. Но́жниц is the genitive plural (па́ра но́жниц), wrong for a subject. As a plural subject the form is simply но́жницы.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Many English people live in our city.
minimalPairs.explanation: Англича́нин drops the -ин syllable in the plural (англича́не) and takes the zero gen pl: англича́н. Англича́нов is a learner's analogical form built on the singular stem - the irregular pattern does not allow it.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I have no money at all.
minimalPairs.explanation: Де́ньги takes a fleeting vowel in the genitive plural to break the unpronounceable cluster -ньг: де́нег. Де́ньг is the bare-cluster trap and does not occur.

sentenceBuilding.hint: Часы is plural-only; after нет use the memorised genitive plural часов.
Джинсы is plural-only and inanimate, so the accusative equals the nominative.

sentenceBuilding.translation: There are many citizens in the square.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Много takes the genitive plural; гражданин drops -ин to the zero ending граждан.
Деньги is plural-only; the genitive plural inserts a fleeting vowel: денег.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each word by which special group it belongs to.

patternRecognition.question: What kind of noun is но́жницы?
patternRecognition.explanation: Но́жницы exists only in the plural; there is no но́жница singular in modern Russian. Plural-only nouns decline as ordinary plurals, but the gen pl (но́жниц) must be memorised because there is no singular to anchor on.

patternRecognition.sentence: По́сле трёх су́ток в доро́ге они́ верну́лись.
patternRecognition.question: Why is the form су́ток here?
options: It is the genitive plural of the plural-only noun су́тки
су́тки is a singular noun here
patternRecognition.answer: It is the genitive plural of the plural-only noun су́тки
patternRecognition.explanation: Су́тки ('a 24-hour day') is a plural-only noun. After трёх (a 5+-type count) the noun is the genitive plural, which for су́тки is the memorised су́ток. There is no singular су́тка to fall back on.

reviewVocab.definition: plural-only nouns (no singular form): часы́, но́жницы, очки́, де́ньги, су́тки, воро́та, штаны́, духи́, кани́кулы, джи́нсы. The gen pl must be memorised: часо́в, но́жниц, очко́в, де́нег, су́ток, воро́т, штано́в, кани́кул.
reviewVocab.example: У меня нет часов. Маша купила новые очки.

reviewVocab.definition: money (plural-only); the genitive plural inserts a fleeting vowel to break the cluster: нет де́нег.
reviewVocab.example: У студентов нет денег. Благодаря деньгам они купили билеты.

reviewVocab.definition: singulars in -анин / -янин drop the -ин syllable in the plural and add -е; the gen pl is zero. Граждани́н → гра́ждане / гра́ждан; англича́нин → англича́не / англича́н; крестья́нин → крестья́не / крестья́н; славяни́н → славя́не / славя́н.
reviewVocab.example: На площади много англичан. В классе сидят русские крестьяне.
